To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the use of plastid- as well as nuclear-encoded reference genes is important to normalize expression levels of plastid- or nuclear-encoded photosynthetic genes, respectively.

1) the best reference genes for normalising photosynthetic genes were found in the plastid and the nucleus, 2) the best reference gene for normalising plastid-encoded photosynthetic genes in Nicotania tabacum is Nt-RPS2, 3) the best reference for normalising nuclear-encoded photosynthetic gene is Nt-ACT8.
plastid-encoded reference genes were more stable than nuclear-encoded genes in N. tabacum.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of appropriate reference genes in Nicotianatabacum for normalization of photosynthesis gene expression in plants with altered cytokinin contents.
the identification of appropriate reference genes for the normalization of gene expression levels in transgenic Nicoti

a strategy for selecting appropriate reference genes for normalization of photosynthesis gene expression, and it provides a useful resource for future studies on the effect of cytokinins or other plant hormones on gene expression in Nicotiana
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
plastid and nuclear reference genes should be used for normalizing plastidal and nuclear encoded photosynthetic genes, respectively.
the best strategy to normalize photosynthetic genes in Nicotania tabacum is the use of plastid and nuclear encoded reference genes.

the use of nuclear-encoded reference genes is not suitable for normalizing plastome-encoded genes, and that the use of plastid- or nuclear-encoded genes for normalising nuclear-encoded genes is not suitable.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the use of a single reference gene is not recommended and that the use of multiple reference genes is necessary for accurate normalization in RT-PCR assays.
the use of nuclear-encoded reference genes only for normalizing photosynthesis gene expression may be misleading.
plastid and nuclear reference genes are not interchangeable and that plastid-encoded reference genes should be preferred for normalization of plastid-encoded target genes.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the choice of reference genes for normalization of RT-PCR data should be made on a case-by-case basis, depending on the type of genes to be quantified and the experimental conditions used.

normalization of plastid- or nuclear photosynthetic gene transcripts with nuclear- or plastid reference genes, respectively, is a more reliable strategy than normalization with nuclear reference genes only.
